newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ROMA SAY DEAL DONE FOR LEVERKUSEN'S SERGIO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMA SAY DEAL DONE FOR LEVERKUSEN'S SERGIO.

text.p: Roma president Francesco Sensi said on Tuesday that his club had agreed with Germany's Bayer Leverkusen on the transfer to Italy of Brazilian midfielder Paulo Sergio.
"Paulo Sergio is Roma's, we have settled," the Ansa news agency quoted Sensi as saying. It said Bayer would receive a payment of around $4 million.

Bayer pulled out of a deal to sell the Brazilian to Roma in March in reaction to a FIFA decision allowing all out-of-contract foreign players to move between clubs within the European Union on free transfers.
Out-of-contract EU nationals had been able to move between clubs in the Union without a transfer fee since the European Court of Justice's "Bosman ruling" of 1995.
But the FIFA decision extended these rights to all players in the EU, regardless of nationality.
Leverkusen, whose sporting director is former Roma player Rudi Voeller, and Roma had agreed on a deal in January for a fee reported to range from $3.6 to $4.6 million.

Under the FIFA ruling, the payment would no longer have been required but Bayer took advantage of a special clause in players' contracts in Germany which allows clubs to retain a player for an extra year if the transfer system changes.
